question: ap1

ideas.title: Stipple test: clonal barcoding of first and second responses
ideas.description: Inspired by the poem's 'rose-moles all in stipple' — a mottled pattern that is stable rather than random — use heritable lineage barcodes (e.g., Watermelon/FateMap-style) to stimulate cells, let them divide through a rest period, then re-stimulate, and ask whether high- and low-responding cells fall into the same clones both times. True AP-1 memory predicts clonally heritable second-response amplitude that correlates with first-response AP-1 target output, whereas a non-memory model predicts clone-independent, resampled variability.

ideas.title: Couple-colour: which Fos/Jun dimer holds the mark
ideas.description: AP-1 is a family of heterodimers, not one protein, so apply subunit-specific degron tags (FOS, FOSL1, JUN, JUNB, ATF3) and deplete each only during the quiescent interval between stimulations, leaving induction itself intact. Pair this with CUT&RUN time courses of each subunit at memory enhancers to distinguish a continuously occupied 'maintenance dimer' from a hit-and-run initiating dimer whose mark is kept by something else.

ideas.title: Swift, slow: decay-constant mismatch between occupancy, accessibility, and output
ideas.description: Memory requires that some layer outlive its input, so measure, in the same time course after a pulsed stimulus, the decay kinetics of AP-1 protein, AP-1 ChIP/CUT&RUN occupancy, ATAC accessibility, H3K4me1/H3K27ac, and nascent transcription at the same loci. The memory signature is a quantitatively slower accessibility half-life than occupancy half-life at a specific enhancer subset; loci where all layers decay together serve as internal negative controls.

ideas.title: Landscape plotted and pieced: synthetic enhancer grammar for persistence
ideas.description: Build an MPRA/synthetic-locus library varying TRE/AP-1 motif number, spacing, affinity, partner-motif identity, and flanking nucleosome-positioning sequence, integrated at a fixed landing pad, then score which designs convert a transient stimulus into weeks-long accessibility and faster re-induction. Validate the top rules by prime-editing the corresponding motifs at endogenous memory enhancers to show that the predicted design features are causally required.

ideas.title: Past change: does the memory survive replication, and who re-writes it?
ideas.description: Test whether the mark is 'past change' through DNA replication by comparing memory retention in cycling versus pharmacologically or contact-arrested cells, and by nascent-chromatin capture (NCC/repli-ATAC) to see whether AP-1 and accessibility are re-established on daughter strands within one cell cycle. Combine with acute MLL3/4, BRD4, or BAF (SMARCA4) inhibition applied only during the rest interval to identify which cofactor actually maintains or re-writes the mark once AP-1 levels have returned to baseline.
